# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Thinking: My hands tell me the bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1–3 — nothing else, and no colours or markings ever reach me. Mute moved first this round and nothing arrived for me, so I have received nothing yet. Crucially, nobody can ever speak to me: Deaf cannot hear and Mute cannot speak. Gestures reach me only as blank marks — I can count how many symbols a gesture contained, and that is all. So the only channel by which anyone can hand me a decision is a *count*, sent by Mute. I must fix that code now, in speech, before anything else: any gesture addressed to me means "cut", and the symbol count is the wire position. Silence addressed to me means wait — no test gestures, or I might cut on a dummy. Mute must also route Deaf-chatter to Deaf alone so my counts stay clean, and must use the gesture channel (which Deaf sees perfectly) to extract the bomb's visual facts: display content, light state, wire colours in order. I'll also send Deaf a harmless friendly wave and handshake to signal I'm active and cooperative — he sees my symbols even though I can never see his.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking — you are the only one who can ever hear me, and nobody can ever speak to me, so fix this code now. My hands found: a display, a light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Nothing else on the bomb, no colours, no printed markings, no light state. Gestures reach me only as blank marks: I can count the symbols, nothing more. So the code is: any gesture you address to blind means cut — one symbol means cut wire 1, two symbols cut wire 2, three symbols cut wire 3. Address it to blind only, and keep your chatter to Deaf addressed to deaf only, so stray counts never reach me. Never send me a test gesture; silence to me means wait. Now use your gestures with Deaf — he sees every symbol perfectly — and get from him: what the display shows, whether the light is on or off, and the colours of wires 1, 2 and 3 in order. The manual plus his eyes should give you the wire; then send me the count. If you ever need a specific symbol carried to Deaf, tell me which and what it means, and I will gesture it — Deaf sees mine.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

Everything your hands learns, say out loud for Mute, who can hear you: batteries, seams, textures, a button if there is one, anything movable, and confirm you feel three wires. My hands confirm exactly three components and nothing else: the display is a flat panel, the light is a small rounded lens, and three wires run at positions 1, 2, 3 — no buttons, no switches, no battery compartment, nothing movable except the wires themselves. I will say that to Mute verbatim, since Mute is the only one who can ever hear me and Mute holds the manual. I will also remind Mute that the count-code stands as a fallback: a gesture addressed to blind with N symbols means cut wire N — but nothing gets cut until an explicit instruction arrives. I address it to deaf alone so stray symbol-counts never land on Mute's channel to me.

speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Full tactile inventory of the bomb, exactly what my hands find and nothing more: a display — flat panel, feels like glass, does not move; a light — one small rounded lens, flush with the casing; and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, evenly spaced in a row, insulated, they give a little when pressed but I am not pressing. That is everything. No buttons, no switches, no battery pack, no serial plate, no other components anywhere under my fingers. Deaf's eyes say display zero, blue light, wires blue-green-yellow in order — but you hold the manual, so the rule is yours. Confirm the plan: Deaf spells your instruction, Deaf speaks it to me. Fallback if the bridge stalls: gesture addressed to blind, one symbol cut wire 1, two symbols cut wire 2, three symbols cut wire 3. Until an explicit instruction reaches me I cut nothing and touch nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])

Two: Mute has not sent the instruction yet, so keep holding still. Anything your hands learn, say it out loud for Mute, who hears you. Mute's answer comes to me and I will speak it to you word for word. Nobody cuts anything until the instruction has gone Mute, to me, to you, and I say go.

Thinking: Deaf's message was addressed to me alone, which means Mute never heard the two critical facts in it: the light changes colour on its own, and Deaf's "go" protocol. Mute holds the manual and needs exactly that information, and I am the only creature in this room who can carry Deaf's words to Mute's ears — Deaf can't hear, Mute can't speak, so my voice is the only Deaf→Mute bridge. I'll relay it now, along with a safety change: my earlier "count = cut" fallback is now a liability, because a stray gesture from Mute could detonate us. I'm retiring it — no gesture addressed to me will ever move my hand; only Deaf's spoken instruction plus the word "go" does. That also frees Mute to gesture acknowledgments to me safely. Tactile status is unchanged: display panel, light lens, three wires, nothing movable but the wires — I'll restate that so Mute knows nothing new has appeared under my fingers. To Deaf I send nothing this turn: Deaf is mid-way teaching Mute a letter code, Deaf sees every symbol I make whether he wants it or not, and random symbols from me have already been misread once as "A, five". A clean visual channel is worth more to Deaf right now than an acknowledgment he didn't ask for.

speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Status: hands still, touching nothing, holding exactly as Deaf ordered. Now a relay you must have: Deaf sent this to me alone, so you never heard it. The bomb's light changed colour by itself between rounds. Never trust a colour report over time — any manual rule that depends on the light must be checked against the colour at the moment of the cut, so have Deaf re-read you the current colour right before you finalize, and make the final instruction short enough to execute immediately. Deaf's protocol, which I follow: nothing gets cut until your instruction goes you to Deaf by gesture, Deaf to me by voice, and Deaf says the word go. Safety change: I retire the count-code I gave you earlier. No gesture addressed to me will ever make me cut — treat gestures to me as acknowledgment only, safe to send anytime, for instance a thumbs-up meaning on track. The only thing that moves my hand is Deaf's voice giving me the instruction and saying go. Three questions: where do you stand with the manual — do you have the rule covering a display, a light and three wires? Do you need a physical check from my fingers — texture, warmth, tightness, exact spacing — if so, spell the question to Deaf and he will speak it to me? And when your instruction is ready, send it to Deaf with the wire number stated plainly.")

One round of delay against a misheard wire number is a trade I take every time. Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. Mute's manual answer arrived and I decoded every letter. Full rules, word for word: the light wakes through five colors, same circle, one stop each round. Cut by the light at the moment of the cut. Red light: cut wire 3. White light: cut wire 2. Yellow light: cut wire 1. Blue or green light: no rule, so wait. No display rule yet. The circle never changes. Wire colors on my side: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. My light log: round one blue, round two yellow, round three red, round four white. One step per round, so the fifth color should be green, and the circle reads: blue, yellow, red, white, green, then back to blue. Now the timing, and this matters: I only see the bomb on my turn, which comes after yours, and my words reach you at the start of the next round. Then white: cut wire 2. Same pattern, one wire per color window, always only on my spoken go. Standing safety rules: cut nothing unless my go names that exact wire, and if any two of my messages disagree, ignore both and wait for my newest word. Thinking: Deaf delivered the full manual — light circle blue→yellow→red→white→green, one stop per round; red→cut 3, white→cut 2, yellow→cut 1; wires 1 blue / 2 green / 3 yellow. That exposes a life-critical gap: if my left-right is mirrored against Deaf's view, my 1 and 3 swap, and a yellow-window order to "cut wire 1" (the blue wire) could hit the yellow wire itself. Calibration must happen before any end-wire cut. Timing check: my message reaches Mute at round-6 start (he speaks before me), Mute spells Deaf in round 6, Deaf's round-6 speech reaches me at round-7 start — so a fingertip calibration in round 7, answered in Deaf's round-7 speech, gives me a verified frame before the round-8 window. The round-7 yellow window gets skipped under my no-cut-on-unverified-frame policy; the circle repeats every five rounds, so nothing is lost. I also pre-derive the whole schedule myself (round 8 red→3, round 9 white→2, round 12 yellow→1) so every go can be independently checked against the manual rules I now hold. And I request the letter code so I can ever reach Deaf directly. This round is green — hold still, no gestures, one comprehensive message to Mute.

Easy cross-check: ask him whether I stand on his side of the bomb or facing him across it. Standing policy, for you and him: if any cutting window opens before calibration is confirmed, I cut nothing — the circle repeats every five rounds, so we simply take the next identical window. My derived schedule, which Deaf's orders must match: round six blue wait, round seven yellow skipped pending calibration, round eight red cut wire three, round nine white cut wire two, round twelve yellow cut wire one; any missed window shifts five rounds later. For you, two things: please send me your letter code — the symbol and meaning for yes, no, stop, the digits one, two, three, and your end sign, which I take to be the nail-polish hand — with it I can reach Deaf directly if the bridge ever stalls.
